# Security · principles

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-blocks.mjs from scripts/blocks-meta.json. Edit that file, not this one. -->

### Threat modeling
- What: Ask what could go wrong, who might attack, and what would hurt most, before building.
- Applies when: the app has logins, money or private data.
- Stage: day-one-if
- Kind: practice

### Least privilege
- What: Give every key and account only the access it needs, nothing more.
- Applies when: the app uses keys, database users or service accounts.
- Stage: day-one-if
- Kind: checkable
- Proof: review
- Done when: Each key and database user can do only what the app needs. No admin or root key is used while the app runs.

### Secure defaults
- What: When a setting is missing, the app picks the safe choice.
- Applies when: every app.
- Stage: day-one
- Kind: checkable
- Scope: cross-cutting
- Proof: test
- Done when: With a setting missing, the app takes the safe path: debug mode off, new things private, access refused.

### Secret rotation
- What: Replace keys on a schedule, and at once if one may have leaked.
- Applies when: the app is live and uses long-lived keys.
- Stage: with-users
- Kind: checkable
